question: What does prevalence measure in a community?

options.A: The total number of existing disease cases
options.B: The number of deaths caused by an illness
options.C: The rate at which a disease spreads rapidly
options.D: The number of new infections starting today

explanation: Prevalence counts all existing cases, both old and new, in a population at a specific time. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T12#GNS313_U1_T12_h1)

question: Why is prevalence data most useful for community health nurses?

options.A: It proves the exact day a patient contracted an illness
options.B: It replaces the need for clinical diagnosis in the field
options.C: It stops new infections from entering the community
options.D: It helps plan long-term care and allocate resources

explanation: Knowing the total burden of disease helps nurses and health planners prepare adequate facilities and supplies. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T12#GNS313_U1_T12_h1)

question: What is point prevalence?

options.A: Tracking the death rate from a single outbreak
options.B: Predicting how long a chronic illness will last
options.C: Calculating new infections over a five-year span
options.D: Measuring disease frequency at one specific moment

explanation: Point prevalence looks at a condition at a single, exact moment in time, like a photograph. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T12#GNS313_U1_T12_h2)

question: How does period prevalence differ from point prevalence?

options.A: It excludes patients who recovered before the study began
options.B: It only counts cases diagnosed by a doctor in a hospital
options.C: It includes cases present at any time during a set interval
options.D: It measures only brand-new infections over a lifetime

explanation: Period prevalence covers a span of time, capturing anyone who had the condition during that entire period. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T12#GNS313_U1_T12_h2)

question: What forms the numerator in the standard prevalence formula?
explanation: The top part of the fraction always represents all existing cases, both old and new, at that moment. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T12#GNS313_U1_T12_h3)

question: A clinic finds 20 people with malaria in a town of 4,000 residents. What is the prevalence per 1,000 people?
explanation: Divide 20 by 4,000 to get 0.005, then multiply by 1,000 to get 5 per 1,000 people. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T12#GNS313_U1_T12_h3)

question: What happens to disease prevalence if a new, highly effective cure is discovered?

options.A: Prevalence doubles because more people will seek testing
options.B: Prevalence increases because cured patients are counted twice
options.C: Prevalence stays the same because cures do not affect statistics
options.D: Prevalence decreases because patients recover and leave the active pool

explanation: Quick recovery removes people from the count of existing cases, driving the prevalence rate down. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T12#GNS313_U1_T12_h4)

question: Which of the following will NOT typically cause prevalence to increase?

options.B: A long duration of the illness
options.C: Migration of sick people into the town
options.D: A high death rate from the disease

explanation: A high mortality rate removes people from the population quickly, which lowers prevalence rather than raising it. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T12#GNS313_U1_T12_h4)

question: What is the main difference between incidence and prevalence?

options.A: Incidence is used for chronic diseases, while prevalence is for injuries
options.B: Incidence counts only new cases, while prevalence counts all existing cases
options.C: Incidence measures past history, while prevalence predicts future risk
options.D: Incidence requires a blood test, while prevalence is calculated by survey

explanation: Incidence tracks newly developing cases, whereas prevalence tracks the total burden of existing cases. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T12#GNS313_U1_T12_h5)

question: A chronic disease has very few new cases each year, yet a high number of people live with it for decades. What will the statistics show?

options.B: Both incidence and prevalence will be equal
options.C: Both incidence and prevalence will be zero

explanation: Few new cases mean low incidence, but long-term survival accumulates existing cases, resulting in high prevalence. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T12#GNS313_U1_T12_h5)

question: A community health nurse notices a high prevalence of type 2 diabetes in a specific neighborhood. What is the most appropriate action?

options.A: Close all local clinics since the population is already quite sick
options.B: Establish targeted screening and lifestyle education posts in that neighborhood
options.C: Transfer all affected patients immediately to a tertiary teaching hospital
options.D: Ignore the data because prevalence only matters for infectious outbreaks

explanation: High prevalence guides nurses to focus local resources, screening, and education where the need is greatest. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T12#GNS313_U1_T12_h6)

question: How do nurses use prevalence data when seeking funding from health ministries?

options.A: To demonstrate the total burden of disease and justify resource requests
options.B: To calculate the exact birth date of every infected community member
options.C: To replace physical examinations during routine home visits
options.D: To prove that no further medical supplies are required in the region

explanation: Showing the total number of people affected helps justify why funding and materials are urgently required. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T12#GNS313_U1_T12_h6)

question: What is a major limitation of relying solely on prevalence studies?

options.A: They are completely illegal to conduct in rural community settings
options.B: They can be affected by survival bias, missing those who died quickly
options.C: They cost more money than any other form of scientific research
options.D: They only measure future health risks and ignore current problems

explanation: Prevalence only counts current survivors, missing individuals who died rapidly before being surveyed. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T12#GNS313_U1_T12_h7)

question: Why might a survey show a very low prevalence for a mild skin condition that many people actually have?

options.A: Mild conditions automatically increase incidence instead of prevalence
options.B: Skin conditions cannot be measured using mathematical fractions
options.C: Government regulations forbid recording mild skin complaints
options.D: People may not seek care or report symptoms because the condition is mild

explanation: Unreported or undiagnosed mild illnesses are missed in surveys, leading to an underestimation of true prevalence. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T12#GNS313_U1_T12_h7)
